name_note: GTDB divides the classical species Rothia mucilaginosa into more than one species, of which s__Rothia mucilaginosa_A is one; the cited work uses the undivided name Rothia mucilaginosa.

sentences.text: Rothia mucilaginosa is an opportunistic Gram-positive coccus that colonizes the oral cavity.
It has also been described as a commensal bacterium with established anti-inflammatory properties in the respiratory tract.

A case series reports that it has emerged as an important opportunistic pathogen, with invasive infections increasingly recognized in immunocompromised patients, including those with haematolymphoid malignancies and neutropenia.
One study reported that its abundance on the lip vermilion inversely correlated with the severity of actinic cheilitis, and that its membrane vesicles contain ferrochelatase.
Its therapeutic potential has been evaluated in a loperamide-induced constipation mouse model, in which mice were treated with the organism and assessed by multiomics.
